Compute alpha- or beta-diversity metrics on a phyloseq object via ecodive

Source: R/diversity_pq.R
diversity_pq.Rd

Wrapper around ecodive::beta_div() and ecodive::alpha_div() providing fast, C-accelerated alpha- and beta-diversity calculations directly on a phyloseq object, plus support for "robust_aitchison" (alias "robust.aitchison").

Usage

diversity_pq(
  physeq,
  metric = "bray",
  norm = "none",
  pseudocount = NULL,
  impute = FALSE,
  add_to_phyloseq = FALSE,
  nproc = 1L,
  ...
)

Arguments

physeq

(required) a phyloseq-class object obtained using the phyloseq package.

metric

(character, default "bray") Name(s) of the diversity metric(s) to compute. See ecodive::list_metrics() for all supported alpha and beta metric IDs, plus "robust_aitchison" (or "robust.aitchison"). All elements of metric must belong to the same family (either all "beta" or all "alpha").

norm

(character, default "none") Normalization passed to ecodive::beta_div() ("none", "percent", "binary", "clr"). For alpha-diversity metrics that require proportions, "none" is mapped to ecodive::alpha_div()'s default "percent".

pseudocount

(numeric or NULL, default NULL) Pseudocount added to counts to handle zeros when metric = "aitchison" or norm = "clr".

impute

(logical, default FALSE) Only used when metric is "robust_aitchison" or "robust.aitchison". If FALSE (default), uses ecodive's zero-filled rCLR Euclidean distance. If TRUE, uses vegan::vegdist(..., method = "robust.aitchison") with OptSpace low-rank matrix completion.

add_to_phyloseq

(logical, default FALSE) Only used for alpha-diversity metrics. If TRUE, appends the computed alpha-diversity columns to physeq@sam_data and returns the updated phyloseq object.

nproc

(integer, default 1L) Number of CPU threads passed to ecodive (cpus). Defaults to 1L to comply with CRAN check limits.

...

Additional arguments forwarded to ecodive::beta_div(), ecodive::alpha_div(), or vegan::vegdist() (when impute = TRUE).

Value

  • For beta-diversity: a stats::dist object when length(metric) == 1, or a named list of stats::dist objects when length(metric) > 1.

  • For alpha-diversity: a tibble::tibble with column Sample and one column per metric (when add_to_phyloseq = FALSE), or a phyloseq object with those columns added to sample_data(physeq) (when add_to_phyloseq = TRUE).

Details

Robust Aitchison distance (metric = "robust_aitchison"): Two definitions exist in the microbiome literature (both citing Martino et al. 2019):

  • impute = FALSE (default, ecodive definition): applies the robust centered log-ratio (rCLR) transformation to strictly positive counts in each sample (log(x) - mean(log(x[x > 0])) for x > 0, and 0 otherwise) and computes the Euclidean distance via ecodive. This avoids pseudocounts and runs in milliseconds in C, without iterative matrix completion.

  • impute = TRUE (DEICODE / vegan OptSpace definition): applies rCLR leaving zeros as NA, completes the low-rank matrix with OptSpace (vegan::decostand() with method = "rclr", impute = TRUE, called by vegan::vegdist(..., method = "robust.aitchison")), and computes the Euclidean distance on the completed matrix. Because vegan already implements OptSpace matrix completion natively, no external rpca dependency is needed.

References

Martino C, Morton JT, Marotz CA, Thompson LR, Tripathi A, Knight R, Zengler K (2019). A novel sparse compositional technique reveals microbial perturbations. mSystems 4(1): e00016-19. doi:10.1128/mSystems.00016-19

See also

ecodive::beta_div(), ecodive::alpha_div(), vegan::vegdist(), hill_pq()

Author

Adrien Taudière

Examples

# \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("ecodive", quietly = TRUE)) {
  pq_5 <- prune_samples(sample_names(data_fungi_mini)[1:5], data_fungi_mini)
  # Beta-diversity (Bray-Curtis and Robust Aitchison)
  diversity_pq(pq_5, metric = "bray")
  diversity_pq(pq_5, metric = "robust_aitchison")

  # Alpha-diversity
  diversity_pq(pq_5, metric = c("shannon", "simpson", "observed"))
}
#> Taxa are now in columns.
#> # A tibble: 5 × 4
#>   Sample                         shannon simpson observed
#>   <chr>                            <dbl>   <dbl>    <dbl>

#> 2 A10-005-H_S189_MERGED.fastq.gz  0.0118 0.00274        5
#> 3 A10-005-M_S190_MERGED.fastq.gz  1.42   0.727          7
#> 4 A12-007_S191_MERGED.fastq.gz    0.506  0.185         10
#> 5 A12-007-B_S2_MERGED.fastq.gz    0.687  0.494          2
